claim: Which figure number belongs to which panel
locus_a: SI p. S1, table of contents: 'Figure S1 Cytotoxicity assay of unsaturated lipidoids ... S2' / 'Figure S2 TEM images of 16II/DNA and 16II/mRNA complexes ... S2' / 'Figure S3 Ethidium bromide (EB) exclusion assay ... S3'
locus_b: the panels' own captions: p. S2 'Figure S1. TEM images of 16II/DNA (A) and 16II/mRNA complexes (B)' and 'Figure S2. Ethidium bromide (EB) exclusion assay of 16I/DNA and 16II/DNA'; p. S3 'Figure S3. Cell variability of HeLa cells upon exposure to unsaturated lipidoids.'
what_we_emitted: Nothing is emitted from this paper at all. Every reference in this folder cites panels by their CAPTION number and says so explicitly (05_values.csv has both `panel` and `panel_per_caption`).
why: The three contents are the same three items, so content-matching is unambiguous - the TOC's TEM line even repeats the caption's '16II/DNA and 16II/mRNA' wording verbatim. Only the NUMBERING is permuted, cyclically by one: TOC says S1=cytotoxicity, S2=TEM, S3=EB while the captions say S1=TEM, S2=EB, S3=viability. The TOC's page is wrong too (it puts cytotoxicity on S2; it is on S3). The caption sits on the panel, so the caption governs.
severity: cosmetic for us, but a real citation hazard: anyone citing 'Figure S1' of this paper means a different panel depending on which page they read.

claim: What the 16-bar panel measures, and what it is called
locus_a: SI p. S1 TOC calls it a 'Cytotoxicity assay'; p. S3 caption calls it 'Cell variability'
locus_b: the panel's own y-axis text layer reads 'Cell Viability (%)' and its values run 66.3-99.5 with no value below 60
what_we_emitted: Recorded as cell viability, non-admissible. 05_values.csv's `assay` field states all three names and that the SI names no assay method (no MTT, MTS or similar appears anywhere in the 3 pages).
why: 'Cell variability' is a typo for 'viability'; the axis label settles it, and values clustered at 66-100 % are viability, not variability. The TOC's 'cytotoxicity' is the same quantity named by its complement. None of the three makes it a delivery endpoint.
severity: does not change a value; it changes what the value IS, which is why it is recorded rather than silently harmonised.

claim: Which of 16I and 16II is the unsaturated lipidoid
locus_a: p. S2 Figure S2 caption lists them in the order '16I/DNA and 16II/DNA'
locus_b: the same figure's legend lists its two series in the order 'Unsaturated Lipidoid' then 'Saturated Lipidoid'
what_we_emitted: NOT ASSIGNED. 01_blocks_qc.json records what is certain (the numeral distinguishes the oleyl series from the n-octadecyl series) and what is not (which numeral is which). See DECISIONS.md D-2.
why: Nothing states that the caption order and the legend order correspond, and the SI defines neither numeral. Two inferences are available and they point OPPOSITE ways: Figure S1 shows 16II with both DNA and mRNA, which looks like the lead compound and so favours 16II = unsaturated (the abstract says unsaturated is superior); but the abstract ascribes the difference to 'the large, tightly packed lipoplexes of SATURATED lipidoids', which is a reason to show a TEM of the saturated one. Guessing would put a label on the wrong series.
severity: would change which structure a value belongs to, if any value were emitted. None is.
